issue: Bank engine has no §15.5 CET1 constraint. Flat 0.75 payout in every world; book equity compounds at 2.6% p.a. against AIEA at 4.35%, so the implied capital ratio falls every year and the model never notices. Stagflation NPAT falls 57.5% with payout unchanged.
treatment: Step 1 IMPLEMENTED 16 Sep 2026 — warn-only, no level moved. src/vcc_valuations/dcf/bank_capital.py projects the CET1 path and the engine appends its warnings. The ratio is anchored on WBC's reported CET1 and rolled forward on the model's own implied rates: equity growth from retained earnings over opening equity, RWA growth from AIEA times a density derived from reported RWA. CET1 is not book equity and the data carries no bridge, so the level is anchored on the observable rather than reconstructed — the diagnostic is therefore exact on direction and rate of drift and indicative on the level at which a threshold is crossed, which is the right trade for a warning. It reproduces the finding: equity compounds at 2.5–2.8% against RWA at 4.35%, and CET1 erodes in every scenario — 97bp on Muddle Through (12.42% to 11.45%, crossing the 11.50% operating target at Y5), 165bp on Orderly Convergence (crossing at Y3), 71bp on Stagflation. None breaches the 10.25% APRA floor inside the explicit period, so this is a board event rather than a regulator event. Zero base-tie risk is structural, not asserted: book equity is a pure accumulator in the §15 build (NII comes from AIEA, never from equity), so the per-period roll-forward sums to the closing figure the terminal value already used. Tested both ways — the same inputs with the capital block stripped give an identical share price. Thresholds come from D-59. Step 2, the forced payout cut, is the outstanding part and needs a ruling — it is the step that moves all six WBC levels. Step 2 RULED, BUILT and SWITCHED ON 16 Sep 2026 as D-60. The payout is cut to hold CET1 on the operating target, one-sided. It raises the valuation rather than lowering it — retention capitalises in the terminal at (ROE-g)/(Ke-g) = 1.54x against a forgone dividend worth about 0.7x, so +0.04 on Muddle Through and +0.66 on Orderly Convergence. That means the model has no interior optimum on payout, which collides with D-45: retention is the derived third of growth, return and reinvestment, and here it moves while terminal ROE and g stay fixed. Left off rather than re-pinning six levels on the artefact. Switched on after Stephen ruled that the rise in value is the retention trade rather than an artefact — lower dividends now for higher dividends later, which the justified P/B form already embeds via g = ROE x b. WBC re-pinned; Fragmentation and Stagflation unchanged because the rule never binds there. Item closed. [Reviewed 16 Oct 2026: Done. The CET1 constraint is on by default (D-60), so the warn-only step is superseded.]

source: Batch 3 item 19, found by the new schema validators
issue: APRA CET1 floor does not reconcile. australian_major_banks.yaml lists regulatory_minimum 8.0% + capital_conservation_buffer 2.5% + countercyclical_buffer 1.0% + d_sib_surcharge 1.0% = 12.5%, against a stated total_floor of 11.5%. The block's own rationale (regionals at 10.5% with no surcharge) implies the countercyclical buffer sits OUTSIDE the stated floor, which reconciles to 11.5%.
treatment: Closed by D-59, 16 Sep 2026 — and the question as recorded was mis-framed. The CCyB is inside the requirement: APS 110 sets it by extending the range of the capital conservation buffer. But the reconciliation the carve-out achieved was hiding a basis error underneath it — regulatory_minimum held the TOTAL capital minimum (Tier 1 plus Tier 2) in a field measured on CET1, and the conservation buffer held the standardised figure for banks that are all IRB. The floor is corrected to the real APRA stack with all four components inside the total, and the figure previously stated as the floor is now declared as what it actually was: an operating target, in its own field, with the management buffer inside the level rather than added on top. A validator now rejects a target at or below its own floor.

issue: WBC's CET1 operating range is superseded, and the block is internally inconsistent. wbc.yaml carries operating_target_range [0.110, 0.115] with commentary "Management target 11.0-11.5% operating range", plus a target_minimum of 0.115 that equals the TOP of that range rather than its bottom, and a management_target of 0.12. Westpac's own disclosure has moved on: the board target is a post-dividend CET1 ratio above 11.25%, stated as replacing the former 11.00-11.50% range, following APRA's phase-out of AT1 from 1 January 2027. Reported Level 2 CET1 was 12.53% at 30 Sep 2025 against the 0.1242 the file carries for 1H26.
treatment: Not changed in passing — it is a company-level domain call and it is the level the §15.5 constraint and the dividend rule will bind on, so it wants Stephen's ruling rather than a session's reading. Two questions: whether the single ">11.25%" target replaces the range outright in the data, and how target_minimum should be re-expressed now that it is neither a minimum nor a floor. The company cet1 block is also untyped — no schema class — which is how the internal inconsistency survived; typing it is the natural companion change. Archetype side is settled under D-59. Now also gates step 2 of item 8: the payout rule needs to know which company-level target it is defending. CLOSED 17 Sep 2026. Stephen ruled the target minimum is 11.25% — Westpac's stated post-dividend board target, which its own disclosure says replaces the 11.00-11.50% range. target_minimum corrected to 0.1125 with a source basis, the range kept as superseded_operating_target_range for history, management_buffer and management_target removed as the third and fourth inconsistent descriptions of the same thing, and current_buffer_bps corrected to 117. The engine now prefers a company's own declared target over the archetype anchor (D-61). Consequence: at 11.25% rather than 11.50%, D-60's payout constraint stops binding in five of six scenarios, so WBC returns to 30.0304 on the central case — the audited v4 workbook figure — and only Orderly Convergence still binds, at Y4.

issue: The declared terminal ROE bears no tested relationship to the ROE the explicit period actually earns. Measured on the final explicit year's NPAT over closing book equity, the gap runs from -0.03pp to -3.00pp on five scenarios (declared below earned, i.e. a conservative fade) — but on Stagflation the declared 9.00% sits 4.01pp ABOVE the 4.99% the final year earns. That is a perpetual recovery assumption, and nothing declares it as one. It matters most precisely there: Stagflation's terminal is 84.45% of the equity claim, the highest in the project, so the worst-case valuation is five-sixths driven by a terminal that assumes ROE almost doubles from where the explicit period leaves it.
treatment: Diagnostic BUILT 16 Sep 2026. src/vcc_valuations/dcf/terminal_return.py computes the terminal return on NEW capital from the growth identity g = return x reinvestment_rate on production engine output, against two benchmarks: the cost of capital (D-42) and the return the final explicit year actually earns (M14). scripts/size_terminal_returns.py regenerates design/methodology/terminal_return_sets.yaml for all 18 valuations and tests/dcf/test_terminal_return_sets.py asserts it, per standing rule 4. The two constructions were lifted from tests/dcf/harness/replica.py rather than reinvented, and moved into the engine path because a number that reaches a document cannot come from a harness (D-51). The M14 finding is confirmed and isolated: WBC Stagflation's declared terminal ROE sits 401bp above the 4.99% its final explicit year earns. Every other WBC scenario is conservative or flat against earned, so this is one scenario's recovery assumption rather than a systemic bias. Still needs Stephen's ruling on whether it is intended and where it should be declared. Return on the WHOLE capital base is not yet reported — FcfEngine carries no invested-capital roll-forward, so it cannot be struck from engine output; that is the natural next step and D-44 already defines the opening base for DNL. D-42 ratified and implemented 17 Sep 2026, and the structured excess_return_defence it introduced is where M14's answer belongs: the decay_horizon basis field is the place to declare a recovery assumption. WBC is baselined for a structural reason rather than an omission — the bank matrix carries no terminal_roic driver for any scenario, because in the §15 fork the terminal return is a declared input on the scenario overlay rather than a matrix cell, so there is nowhere for a bank defence to live until that is decided. 17 Sep: the whole-capital reading is now reported for DNL and the declared rate is reconcilable, which surfaced M16. WBC still cannot report it — the §15 fork has no invested-capital construction at all. [Reviewed 16 Oct 2026: Diagnostic built (dcf/terminal_return.py). The decision on the terminal return is still open.] Closed 16 Oct 2026: superseded by D-65's mechanism, as recorded in the 24 Sep ratification note in DECISIONS.md.
questions: Two now. (1) Is Stagflation's terminal ROE 4pp above its final earned year intended as a recovery, and what is its basis? (2) Where does a BANK's terminal-return defence live, given the terminal ROE is a scenario-overlay input rather than an impact-matrix driver?

issue: CSL's terminal asserts a 61-73% return on new capital, and that is D-53 unimplemented. The segment terminal declares terminal_capex_pct_revenue: 0.06 equal to da_pct_revenue: 0.06, so net capex in the terminal is exactly zero and the only reinvestment left is working capital at g x 0.35, about 1.05% of revenue. A perpetuity growing at 3% while reinvesting roughly 4% of its earnings is asserting a return on new capital in the high sixties against a discount rate of 8.75% — an excess of 5,258 to 6,415bp depending on scenario. For comparison, DNL now runs 4.85% to 12.13% against a WACC of 8.88%, which is the range a real business occupies.
treatment: This is not a new defect — it is the quantification D-53 was missing. D-49 retired capex_rule: equals_da as a house rule on the argument that capex equal to depreciation holds the asset base flat in nominal dollars while revenue compounds; D-53 ruled that argument general and therefore applicable to CSL. Implementing D-53 raises CSL's terminal capex above D&A, cuts terminal FCFF and lowers all six CSL levels, and should drop the implied return into the range DNL occupies. The diagnostic gives that implementation a target to land in and a before-figure to cite. Take with D-55, which also moves all six CSL levels. [Reviewed 16 Oct 2026: Still open. CSL terminal capex equals D&A at 6% of revenue (csl.yaml), so net terminal capex is zero.] [Closed 16 Oct 2026, D-85: the capex line feeds only a diagnostic, so no CSL value moves. The open question is the starting return and fade, now item R16-8.]

issue: D-45 and D-49 both derive reinvestment, from different things, and they do not agree. D-45 says that of terminal growth, terminal return and reinvestment only two are free: g from the macro work, ROIC from the Porter and moat work, and reinvestment derived from them. D-49 says terminal capex is depreciation plus g times the capital base — which derives reinvestment from the balance sheet and leaves the return to emerge. They are consistent only where the declared terminal return equals terminal earnings over the rolled-forward capital base. Now measured for the first time: DNL Orderly Convergence declares 9.13% and the capital build produces 12.46% on the whole base — a gap of 333bp. The declared figure is not an invention: the impact matrix declares terminal_roic as direction positive, magnitude small, and the project's own translation table maps positive-small on a rate driver to +25bp over the convergence target named in the same rationale. So the moat work's view is +25bp and the model delivers +358bp.
treatment: The engine implements D-49, which is why this went unnoticed: terminal_roic existed as a driver with its own basis-point delta convention and no engine ever read it, so the moat work's view was recorded and discarded. The diagnostic now reports both readings and warns on the gap, so it cannot be discarded again. Resolving it is a ruling: either the declared return governs and reinvestment is derived from it (D-45, which makes the moat analysis load-bearing and a defended exception a precondition rather than an audit), or the capital construction governs and the declared return is a cross-check that must be corrected to match (D-49, which keeps the balance-sheet discipline and demotes the Porter work to commentary). Either way the other decision needs amending, and on the central case the choice is worth a large part of the terminal — 70% of DNL's EV sits behind it. [Reviewed 16 Oct 2026: Still open. The engine follows D-49. D-45 disagrees.] Closed 16 Oct 2026: D-62 and D-65 settle it. D-49 supplies the capital base; nothing else declares a terminal return.
questions: Which governs the terminal return: the rate the moat work declares (D-45) or the capital base the explicit period leaves behind (D-49)? And should D-42's obligation carry a materiality floor? DNL Fragmentation triggers it on a 4bp excess, which is the convergence target reached to within rounding rather than a claim about a moat.
